newsitem.title: AZERBAIJAN: Council of Europe tentatively backs Azerbaijan.
newsitem.headline: Council of Europe tentatively backs Azerbaijan.

text.p: A top official of the Council of Europe told Azerbaijan on Thursday she was ready to support the former Soviet republic's bid to join the grouping but that the final decision was not up to her.

On a visit to Baku, Leni Fischer, chairwoman of the Council's assembly, met Foreign Minister Hasan Hasanov and President Haydar Aliyev to discuss entry for Azerbaijan into the 39-nation body, which promotes democracy and human rights.
"I am ready to support Azerbaijan in the question of entering the Council of Europe," Fisher told reporters.
"However a final decision will be taken into account information which will be brought from Azerbaijan by a delegation of experts from the Council of Europe," she added.
Fischer said the delegation would visit Azerbaijan soon but gave no specific date.

Aliyev said he hoped Fischer's visit would speed Azerbaijan's entry into the organisation. "We have done a lot towards democratisation of society and intend to extend these steps in the future," he said.
Aliyev did not elaborate on what had been done to improve Azerbaijan's human rights record, which has come under fire from international organisations.

The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) said after parliamentary elections in November 1995 that the opposition had been discriminated against and some human rights groups have criticised restrictions on the media.
"I am happy with the attention which the Council of Europe is paying to Azerbaijan. We have done quite a lot so that we can join," Aliyev said.

He also said he backed moves by the Council of Europe to bring peace to the volatile Caucasus region, which has been torn by a series of conflicts affecting Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan and Russia. None of them have been fully resolved.
